Measure a search against papers you already know are relevant

Source: R/doc-records-recall.R
gr_search_recall.Rd

Known-item recall: the share of a seed set of relevant papers that a search returned. Each seed is matched to the search's records by the rules gr_records() uses to find duplicates, so a seed counts as found when those rules would call it the same work as one of the records. The figure comes with an exact (Clopper-Pearson) interval from hr_prop_ci(), overall and for each tier when tier is given.

Usage

gr_search_recall(records, known, tier = NULL, held_out = NULL, conf = 0.95)

Arguments

records

The search's results: a gr_records(), or a data frame with its columns (title, year, doi, authors and venue are the ones used). Every row counts, duplicates included.

known

The seed set: a gr_records() read from an export of the papers, or a data frame with doi, or title and year, and where it has them authors and venue. A logical used_to_build column marks the seeds used to write the search. An empty seed set is refused. A row whose duplicate_of names another seed's record_id (two exports of one paper, as gr_records() marks them) is a copy of that seed: the paper is counted once, as used to build the search when any copy is, and the copy is listed in $copies.

tier

NULL, the name of a column of known, or one value per seed: a grouping set by a person (say, core papers and the rest), to report recall for each group as well as overall. A single string is always read as a column name, even with one seed. A seed without a tier, a tier with no seed (an unused factor level), a tier left with no seed once the seeds used to build the search are out, and copies of one paper given different tiers are refused.

held_out

NULL, or the seeds kept out of the search: a logical vector with one value per seed, or their row numbers. Every other seed is counted as used to build the search. A seed marked both held_out and used_to_build is refused.

conf

Confidence level of the intervals.

Value

An object of class gr_search_recall:

recall

One row for all seeds (tier is "all") and one per tier: found, n (seeds counted), estimate, lower, upper, method ("clopper_pearson") and conf.

seeds

One row per distinct seed: seed (its row in known), label, tier, used_to_build, found (NA for a seed left out), record_id (the record it matched) and reason.

missed

The seeds counted and not found, with reason.

refused

The missed seeds the matching rules refused, as described above.

excluded

The seeds left out as used to build the search.

copies

The rows of known that are copies of another seed: seed (the copy's row) and copy_of (the row it is a copy of).

note

The sentence saying what the figure is relative to.

Details

Nothing here calls a model.

Relative recall

The figure is recall relative to the seed set: the share of the papers you already knew that the search found, not the share of every relevant paper that exists. Seeds are rarely a random sample of the relevant literature. They tend to be the well-known, well-indexed papers a search finds most easily, so the figure is usually higher than recall against everything relevant. Report it as relative recall, with the number of seeds and how they were chosen, as PRISMA-S asks a review to describe how its search was tested.

A seed used to write the search (to pick its terms, or to test drafts of it) is found because the search was built to find it. Mark those with a logical used_to_build column in known, or give the seeds kept out of the search in held_out. They are left out of the figure and listed in $excluded.

Seeds that cannot be matched

A seed is matched exactly as gr_records() merges duplicates (see its dedupe argument, "doi+title"): by DOI, or by title and year with the first author or the venue agreeing. Where those rules refuse a match, the seed counts as not found, and $missed says why in reason:

"short_title"

A record has the seed's title and year, but the title has fewer than 12 letters or digits ("Reply", "Editorial"), which the rules never match on.

"multi_doi"

Records with the seed's title and year carry two or more different DOIs between them and the seed, so the title cannot say which work the seed is.

"not_confirmed"

A record has the seed's title and year, but the first author or the venue disagrees, nothing beyond the title confirms it, or it could be either of two records.

"no_identifier"

The seed has no DOI and no title with a year.

"not_in_records"

No record has the seed's DOI, or its title and year.

The first three are listed again in $refused: a search that returned the paper under another record can show as a miss there, and a person should look at those rows before the figure is reported.

References

Sampson, M., Zhang, L., Morrison, A., Barrowman, N. J., Clifford, T. J., Platt, R. W., Klassen, T. P. and Moher, D. (2006). An alternative to the hand searching gold standard: validating methodological search filters using relative recall. BMC Medical Research Methodology 6, 33.

Rethlefsen, M. L., Kirtley, S., Waffenschmidt, S., Ayala, A. P., Moher, D., Page, M. J., Koffel, J. B. and PRISMA-S Group (2021). PRISMA-S: an extension to the PRISMA Statement for Reporting Literature Searches in Systematic Reviews. Systematic Reviews 10, 39.

Clopper, C. J. and Pearson, E. S. (1934). The use of confidence or fiducial limits illustrated in the case of the binomial. Biometrika 26(4), 404-413.

See also

gr_records(), gr_search(), gr_audit_report(), hr_prop_ci()

Examples

found <- data.frame(
  title = c("Spaced practice and long-term retention in adults",
            "Retrieval practice in the classroom: a field trial",
            "Interleaving mathematics problems improves test scores"),
  year = c("2019", "2021", "2015"),
  doi = c("10.1000/sp1", NA, "10.1000/il3"),
  authors = c("Smith, J.", "Okafor, A.", "Lee, K."),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
seeds <- data.frame(
  title = c("Spaced practice and long-term retention in adults",
            "Retrieval practice in the classroom: a field trial",
            "Sleep and memory consolidation in students",
            "Interleaving mathematics problems improves test scores"),
  year = c("2019", "2021", "2020", "2015"),
  doi = c(NA, NA, "10.1000/sl9", "10.1000/il3"),
  authors = c("Smith, J.", "Okafor, A.", "Diaz, M.", "Lee, K."),
  used_to_build = c(FALSE, FALSE, FALSE, TRUE),
  tier = c("core", "core", "other", "other"),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
r <- gr_search_recall(found, seeds, tier = "tier")
r
#> <gr_search_recall> 2 of 3 seed(s) found among 3 record(s)
#>   all              2/3    66.7%  [9.4%, 99.2%]
#>   core             2/2   100.0%  [15.8%, 100.0%]
#>   other            0/1     0.0%  [0.0%, 97.5%]
#>   (95% Clopper-Pearson intervals)
#>   Recall is relative to the seed set: the share of the papers already known
#>   to be relevant that the search found, not the share of every relevant
#>   paper.
#>   1 seed(s) used to build the search are left out (see $excluded)
#>     missed: Diaz 2020: Sleep and memory consolidation in students (not_in_records)
r$missed
#>   seed                                                 label  tier
#> 1    3 Diaz 2020: Sleep and memory consolidation in students other
#>   used_to_build found record_id         reason
#> 1         FALSE FALSE        NA not_in_records
